sections.heading: 1. Speed
points: **Speed** = the **distance travelled per unit time**: **Speed = Distance ÷ Time**.
**SI unit of speed = metre per second (m/s)**; also km/h.
**Uniform motion** — equal distances in equal intervals of time (constant speed).
**Non-uniform motion** — unequal distances in equal intervals (changing speed).

sections.heading: 2. Measuring Time
points: Early clocks used the **repetitive (periodic) motion** — e.g. **sundials, water clocks, sand clocks**.
**Galileo** noticed that a **simple pendulum** swings with a fixed rhythm → basis of **pendulum clocks**.
Modern clocks/watches use **quartz** (very accurate).

sections.heading: 3. The Simple Pendulum
points: A **simple pendulum** = a small metal ball (**bob**) hung by a thread from a fixed point.
One complete to-and-fro swing = one **oscillation**.
**Time period** = the time taken for **one oscillation**; it is **constant** for a given pendulum.
The time period depends on the **length** of the pendulum (not on the bob's mass).

sections.heading: 4. Instruments and Graphs
points: **Speedometer** shows the **speed** of a vehicle (km/h); **odometer** shows the **distance** travelled.
**Distance–time graph:** time on the x-axis, distance on the y-axis.
A **straight line** on a distance–time graph = **uniform motion**; a horizontal line = **at rest**; a curve = non-uniform motion.
Units: 1 km = 1000 m; 1 h = 3600 s.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Speed = distance ÷ time; SI unit = m/s.
Uniform motion = equal distance in equal time; non-uniform = unequal.
Pendulum: oscillation = one to-and-fro swing; time period = time for one oscillation (constant).
Speedometer = speed; odometer = distance.
Distance–time graph: straight line = uniform motion; horizontal = at rest.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **SI unit of speed = m/s** (not km/h).
**Speedometer** measures speed; **odometer** measures distance — don't swap.
A pendulum's **time period** depends on its **length**, not the bob's mass.
On a distance–time graph, a **horizontal line** means the object is **at rest** (not moving fastest).
